fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵拉姆努尔夫一世

sourceNote: The claim to be King of Aquitaine was short-lived and contested.
notes: Son of Ramnulf I; father of the genealogical Ramnulf III branch and of the illegitimate Ebalus.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵拉姆努尔夫二世

sourceNote: Genealogical entry; dates and detailed biography are not securely established in the cited overview.
notes: Shown as a branch of Ramnulf II in the House of Poitiers genealogy, not as the direct father of Ebalus.

sourceNote: Wikipedia identifies Ebalus as the illegitimate son of Ranulf II; the exact maternal line is not supplied here.

fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵埃布勒斯·曼泽尔

fullName: Guilhem III Towhead, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Wikipedia notes that he was called Count of the Duchy of Aquitaine or Count Palatine, but not unambiguously Duke of Aquitaine.
notes: Occitanized display name; English and French forms remain in alsoKnownAs.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆三世·秃头

fullName: Guilhem IV Fierabras, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: The numbering differs between the counts of Poitiers and dukes of Aquitaine.
notes: Occitanized display name; Fierabras means strong-armed/iron arm in the traditional epithet.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆四世·铁臂

fullName: Guilhem V the Great, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: The Ramnulfid overview identifies William V as the father of William VI, Odo, William VII and William VIII branches.
notes: Important patron of learning and culture in Aquitaine; do not collapse his four sons into a single succession chain.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆五世·大公

fullName: Guilhem VI the Fat, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Dates are incomplete in the cited overview.
notes: Eldest son of William V; count of Poitiers from 1030 to 1038.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵吉勒姆六世·肥胖者

fullName: Odo of Gascony, Count of Poitiers
sourceNote: Half-brother of William VI according to the Ramnulfid genealogy.
notes: A collateral succession branch; not the father of William VII or William VIII.
fullNameCn: 普瓦捷伯爵加斯科涅的奥多

sourceNote: Also known as Peter William; half-brother of William VI and William VIII.
notes: The direct dynastic line to Guilhem IX runs through his brother Guilhem VIII, not through Guilhem VII.
fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆七世

sourceNote: Born Gui-Geoffroi; younger brother of William VII and father of William IX.
notes: Occitanized display name Guilhem VIII; the direct father link to existing Guilhem IX is now represented by UUID.
fullNameCn: 阿基坦公爵吉勒姆八世

fullName: Hugues Capet, King of the Franks
sourceNote: Founder of the Capetian dynasty; the direct line here follows the father-to-son succession to Louis VII.
notes: Elected King of the Franks in 987; ancestor of the French royal line represented by Louis VII.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王雨果·卡佩

fullName: Robert II, King of the Franks
sourceNote: Son and successor of Hugh Capet; father of Henry I of France.
notes: Known as Robert the Pious; his reign continued the early Capetian succession.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王罗贝尔二世

fullName: Henri I, King of the Franks
sourceNote: Son of Robert II and father of Philip I of France.
notes: The French form Henri is used for the Capetian canonical display name; Henry I remains an English alias.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王亨利一世

fullName: Philippe I, King of the Franks
sourceNote: Son of Henry I and father of Louis VI of France.
notes: The French form Philippe is used for the canonical display name; Philip I remains an English alias.
fullNameCn: 法兰克人国王腓力一世

fullName: Louis VI, King of the Franks

fullName: Philippe II Augustus, King of France
sourceNote: First Capetian ruler to style himself King of France (Rex Franciae) from about 1190; the usage became established in royal documents by 1204.

fullNameCn: 法兰西国王腓力二世·奥古斯都

fullName: Adèle of Champagne, Queen of France
sourceNote: Third wife of Louis VII and mother of Philip II Augustus.

notes: Her later Byzantine marital history is represented in source notes until spouse cards and cross-realm relationship records are added.
fullNameCn: 法兰西公主阿涅丝
